## 4. Common Administrative Rejection Risks

Use only risks that are supported by the document type, issuing authority, destination, or receiving-authority instructions.

Examples where applicable:

- incomplete or mismatched notarial certificate
- wrong issuing/authentication authority
- document copy used where an original/certified copy is required
- name discrepancy across supporting records
- missing receiving-authority instruction
- incomplete translation/certification requirement
- expired or stale supporting record where the recipient imposes currency requirements
- courier or return-label mismatch

Do not present generalized risks as mandatory legal requirements.

## 6. Milano Seal Coordination Scope

The Milano Seal may coordinate, when applicable and approved for the Matter:

- U.S. document execution
- Remote Online Notarization or in-person/mobile coordination
- apostille or authentication coordination
- document-readiness review
- receiving-authority instruction capture
- translation coordination when separately confirmed
- courier / chain-of-custody handling
- status updates and professional-partner handoff

The Milano Seal does not provide legal advice, legal representation, or guarantees of acceptance by a foreign authority.

## Internal operator controls — do not include in client packet

Before sending:

- verify every country/document statement against current approved sources
- remove internal pricing, margin, payout, confidence enums, and manual-review reasons
- confirm no client from another Matter appears in the packet
- confirm the packet contains no secrets or infrastructure details
- preserve Matter-specific provenance internally
- record the professional-partner touchpoint in the relationship/referral system where supported
